---
title: "Install & set up"
description: "Everything you need on your computer to run the examples: R, Python, Git, Positron, and this repository."
---

This takes about 30 to 60 minutes the first time, and you only do it once per computer. Follow the steps in order. Steps 1 to 3 and 5 to 7 end with a quick check, and step 8 checks everything at the end.

::: {.callout-note}
## 💡 In plain language
**R** and **Python** are the programming languages that do the statistics. **Positron** is the app you type code into. **Git** downloads this repository (a folder of code and data) and later brings it up to date. **uv** installs Python and its add-on packages. The **terminal** is a window where you type commands: **Terminal** on a Mac (press Cmd+Space, type "Terminal" and press Return), **PowerShell** on Windows (open the Start menu, type "PowerShell" and press Enter).
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Just want to read?
You don't need to install anything to read this site. Install only when you're ready to run code yourself.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Before you start

- **Disk space:** about 5 GB free, for R, Python, Positron, the packages and, on a Mac, Apple's command-line tools.
- **Time and internet:** about 30 to 60 minutes, with an internet connection. Steps 1 to 7 each download something.
- **R 4.6:** the tutorials are tested with R 4.6, and the checks in steps 6 and 8 expect it. Step 1 says how to get it.
- **Mac:** R 4.6 needs macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer on a Mac with an Apple chip (M1, M2, …), and macOS 11 (Big Sur) or newer on an Intel Mac. **Apple menu → About This Mac** shows both. If a Mac with an Apple chip has an older macOS, update macOS first: Apple's page [Update macOS on Mac](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108382) says how.
- **Administrator rights:** the installers may ask for an administrator password.
- **HFR computer (laptop or desktop):** install the software on the computer's own disk (`C:`), not on a network drive: Git installed on a network drive can't download the repository (see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)). If an installation fails with an error, contact HFR IT for help.
- **Windows:** the Windows steps follow Microsoft's and Positron's documentation; we haven't run them on a Windows PC ourselves yet. If a step doesn't match what you see, tell us with **Report an error** on this page.
:::

## 1. Install R {#install-r}

The tutorials need R 4.6: any version whose number starts with 4.6, such as 4.6.2.

1. Go to <https://cloud.r-project.org>.
2. Click **Download R for macOS** or **Download R for Windows**.
   - **Mac:** pick the installer for your chip. Apple menu → **About This Mac**: "Apple M…" means *Apple silicon (arm64)*, and "Intel" means *Intel (x86_64)*.
   - **Windows:** click **base**, then the download link at the top of the page.

   The file's name must start with `R-4.6`. If it starts with a higher number, such as `R-4.7`, take R 4.6 from CRAN's earlier versions instead: see the R version row under [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).
3. Open the downloaded file and accept the defaults. The installer may ask for an administrator password. On a Mac, if macOS asks whether the installer may open files in your Downloads folder, allow it: CRAN's download page says you can't install from there otherwise.

**Check:** in step 6, Positron's Interpreter picker shows R 4.6. On a Mac you can also open Terminal and type `R --version`: the first line starts with `R version 4.6`.

## 2. Install uv and Python {#install-uv-and-python}

**Mac:** open Terminal and run:

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

**Windows:** open PowerShell and run:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
```

Close the window, open a new one, and install Python:

```bash
uv python install 3.13
```

**Check:** `uv --version` prints a version number.

## 3. Install Git {#install-git}

- **Mac:** in Terminal, run `xcode-select --install` and click **Install**. This installs Apple's command-line tools, which include Git.
- **Windows:** download Git from <https://git-scm.com/downloads> and accept the defaults. At HFR, when the installer asks where to install Git, make sure the folder is on `C:`, not on a network drive such as `K:`.

**Check:** `git --version` prints a version number.

Prefer not to install Git? Skip this step and download the repository as a ZIP file in step 5 ([Without Git](#zip)). On a Mac, read the note there first.

## 4. Install Positron {#install-positron}

Download Positron from <https://positron.posit.co> and install it like any other app. Positron runs R and Python side by side. Prefer RStudio or VS Code? See [Other editors](#other-editors).

- **Mac:** the download page offers one installer for Apple silicon (M-series) and one for Intel. Pick the one for your chip, as in step 1.
- **Windows:** the download page offers installers for two kinds of processor, x64 (Windows 10 or 11) and ARM64 (Windows 11), each as a *User install* or a *System install*. To see your processor, open **Settings → System → About**: if the *System type* line under *Device specifications* contains the word "ARM", take an ARM64 installer. The x64 installers are for Windows 10 or 11 on an x64 processor. By default, according to Positron's documentation, a user install goes into your own user folder (`C:\Users\<your user name>\AppData\Local\Programs\Positron`) and installs updates in the background; a system install goes into `C:\Program Files\Positron`, and when an update is available Positron downloads it and shows a notice at the bottom left.

## 5. Get this repository {#get-this-repository}

No Git? Use the ZIP file instead: see [Without Git](#zip) below.

In Terminal (Mac) or PowerShell (Windows), make a `projects` folder and download ("clone") the repository into it:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/projects
cd ~/projects
git clone https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation.git
```

`~` stands for your home folder, the folder named after your user name: `/Users/<your user name>` on a Mac, and usually `C:\Users\<your user name>` on Windows. The repository is now in the `projects` folder inside it. To see it on a Mac, click the desktop, then choose **Go → Home** in the menu bar (or press Shift-Command-H): Finder opens your home folder, and `projects` is in it.

Use a folder that is **not** synced to the cloud. `Documents` and `Desktop` are often synced by iCloud (Mac) or OneDrive (Windows). Syncing slows down, and can break, the R and Python environments that steps 6 and 7 create.

Then, in Positron: **File → Open Folder…**, go to your home folder (the folder named after your user name; on a Mac, press Shift-Command-H in the dialog to jump there), open `projects` and choose `stats-formation`.

**Check:** `git clone` starts with `Cloning into 'stats-formation'...` and prints no line that starts with `fatal`. If it prints one, look for it under [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting). In Positron, the file list on the left (click the Explorer icon if you don't see it) shows the repository's folders, among them `data` and `scripts`.

### Without Git: download a ZIP file {#zip}

You don't need Git for this site, and neither route needs a GitHub account. Instead of step 3 and the commands above:

1. Download the repository as a ZIP file: [stats-formation-main.zip](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/archive/refs/heads/main.zip).
2. Unzip it. On a Mac, double-click the file: the folder `stats-formation-main` appears next to it. On Windows, right-click the file, choose **Extract All** and follow the instructions.
3. Move the `stats-formation-main` folder that directly holds `data` and `scripts` into the `projects` folder in your home folder. The ZIP file holds one folder of that name: if unzipping gives you a `stats-formation-main` folder with only another `stats-formation-main` folder inside, use the inner one. If you don't have a `projects` folder yet, make one in your home folder first: on a Mac, choose **Go → Home** in Finder, then **File → New Folder** (or press Shift-Command-N), type `projects` and press Return; on Windows, make it in your home folder, usually `C:\Users\<your user name>`. Don't make it inside a synced folder (see above).
4. In Positron: **File → Open Folder…**, go to your home folder (the folder named after your user name; on a Mac, press Shift-Command-H in the dialog to jump there), open `projects` and choose `stats-formation-main`.

Steps 6 to 8 are the same; only the folder's name differs. The ZIP file holds the site as it is today: [Updating your copy](#updating) says how to get a newer one.

**On a Mac:** this route was tested on a Mac that already had Apple's command-line tools (step 3 installs them). If your Mac asks you to install them during step 6, click **Install**, and run step 6 again when the installation has finished.

**Check:** Positron's file list on the left shows the repository's folders, among them `data` and `scripts`.

## 6. Install the R packages {#install-the-r-packages}

Positron starts R by itself when it opens a folder with a `renv.lock` file, as this one has. The **Interpreter picker**, at the top right of the Positron window, shows the session that is running, for example R 4.6.2. If it shows no R, or an R that isn't 4.6, click the Interpreter picker, choose **New Console Session…** and pick R 4.6 from the list. Because R starts inside the repository folder, it switches on this project's package list. Then, in the **Console** pane, run:

```r
renv::restore()
```

Answer **Y** if asked. This installs every R package the tutorials use, at the exact versions we tested. It takes a few minutes.

**Check:** the output ends without a line that starts with `Error`. To be sure, run `renv::status()` in the same console: it answers `No issues found -- the project is in a consistent state.` When R starts in this folder for the first time, it may print `Bootstrapping renv` and `One or more packages recorded in the lockfile are not installed.` Both are expected before `renv::restore()` has run. If `renv::status()` says `The lockfile was generated with R 4.6.0, but you're using R …`, see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).

## 7. Install the Python packages {#install-the-python-packages}

Open Positron's terminal (**Terminal → New Terminal**). It opens in the repository folder. Run:

```bash
uv sync
```

This creates a private Python environment in the `.venv` folder with every package the tutorials use. Then start a Python console that uses it: click the **Interpreter picker**, choose **New Console Session…** and pick the Python whose path includes `.venv`.

Positron may offer some of this itself. When it opens a folder that has a `uv.lock` file, as this one does, but no `.venv` folder yet, it may offer to run `uv sync` and then select the new environment: accepting runs the same `uv sync` as above. Once `.venv` exists, it may offer to start a console session with it: accepting does the same as the Interpreter picker route.

**Check:** the first time, `uv sync` prints `Creating virtual environment at: .venv`, then one line for each package it installed, starting with `+`. No line starts with `error`. If the environment already exists and is up to date (for example because you accepted Positron's offer), `uv sync` prints just two lines, one starting with `Resolved` and one starting with `Checked`. If some packages were missing, as can happen after an update, it lists the ones it installed in lines starting with `+`.

## 8. Check that everything works {#check-that-everything-works}

In Positron's terminal, run both checks:

```bash
Rscript scripts/check_setup.R
uv run python scripts/check_setup.py
```

Each check ends with `All good - you are ready.` If a line says `PROBLEM`, it tells you what to do. Fix it and run the check again. Midway through, the R check may print three lines that begin `Registered S3 method overwritten by 'lme4':`. That is a note, not a problem: two packages, lme4 and car, both provide the same small function, and R says which one it keeps.

On Windows, if `Rscript` is "not recognized", run the R check from Positron's R console instead:

```r
source("scripts/check_setup.R")
```

## Updating your copy {#updating}

The site changes now and then. To bring your copy up to date:

- **If you cloned it with Git:** in Positron's terminal, in the repository folder, run `git pull`. If nothing has changed, it prints `Already up to date.` (or the same in your system's language). Your practice files in `scratch/` stay as they are, because Git ignores that folder.
- **If you downloaded the ZIP file:** first copy anything of your own out of the old `stats-formation-main` folder, such as the `scratch/` folder. Then download the ZIP file again ([Without Git](#zip)), unzip it, put the new `stats-formation-main` folder in `projects` in place of the old one, and open it in Positron (**File → Open Folder…**). Then copy your own files back into the new folder's `scratch/` folder.

Either way, then run steps 6 to 8 again. After `git pull`, `renv::restore()` and `uv sync` install whatever changed. A fresh ZIP copy has no packages yet, so they install every package again; that is much quicker than the first time, because your computer has kept the downloaded packages.

## Reading the data without cloning {#reading-the-data-without-cloning}

You can skip steps 5 to 8 and read the practice data straight from GitHub, for example to use it in a project of your own. You still need R (step 1) or uv and Python (step 2), and the packages below.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
install.packages(c("readr", "readxl"))   # once

cohort <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/main/data/cohort.csv")
```

## Python

Start Python with the packages it needs. In a terminal:

```bash
uv run --with pandas --with openpyxl python
```

Then:

```python
import pandas as pd

cohort = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/main/data/cohort.csv")
```
:::

Every CSV works the same way: replace `"data/"` with `"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/main/data/"`. To run a whole example from a tutorial page, clone the repository instead (steps 5 to 7): the pages use many more packages than these, and cloning installs them all at the versions we tested.

Excel files are different. R's `read_excel()` can't read a web address, so download the file first. Python's `pd.read_excel()` can read the address directly.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/main/data/messy_abstraction_workbook.xlsx"
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
download.file(url, path, mode = "wb")   # "wb" keeps the file intact on Windows
site_a <- readxl::read_excel(path, sheet = "Site A")
```

## Python

```python
import pandas as pd

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/main/data/messy_abstraction_workbook.xlsx"
site_a = pd.read_excel(url, sheet_name="Site A")
```
:::

### Every data file {#data-files}

Each link below gets one file. An Excel file downloads. A CSV file opens as text in your browser: to save it, right-click the link and choose the command that saves the linked file. Every file is synthetic, like all the data on this site.

Each tidy dataset has a codebook that lists its columns: what each one means, its type, its units and the values it may hold. A codebook link opens on GitHub, which shows the codebook as a table.

| File | One row per | Codebook |
|------|------|------|
| [`data/cohort.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/cohort.csv) | case (one primary hip or knee replacement) | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/cohort.csv) |
| [`data/proms_long.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/proms_long.csv) | case and visit | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/proms_long.csv) |
| [`data/matched_sets.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/matched_sets.csv) | case in a matched set of three | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/matched_sets.csv) |
| [`data/radiographic_reliability.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/radiographic_reliability.csv) | knee, rater and session | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/radiographic_reliability.csv) |
| [`data/hip_fracture.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/hip_fracture.csv) | patient aged 65 or over with a hip fracture | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/hip_fracture.csv) |
| [`data/foot_ankle_rct.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/foot_ankle_rct.csv) | randomized patient | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/foot_ankle_rct.csv) |
| [`data/foot_ankle_rct_long.csv`](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/raw/main/data/foot_ankle_rct_long.csv) | randomized patient and visit | [codebook](https://github.com/hfr-ortho/stats-formation/blob/main/data/codebooks/foot_ankle_rct_long.csv) |

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

| You see | Do this |
|------|------|
| `You have not agreed to the Xcode license` (Mac, during `renv::restore()`) | In Terminal, run `sudo xcodebuild -license accept` and type your Mac password. Then run `renv::restore()` again. |
| `there is no package called 'renv'` | In the R console, run `install.packages("renv")`. Then restart R: open the Command Palette (Cmd+Shift+P on a Mac, Ctrl+Shift+P on Windows), type `Interpreter: Restart Active Interpreter Session` and press Return (Mac) or Enter (Windows). Then run `renv::restore()` again. |
| `The lockfile was generated with R 4.6.0, but you're using R …` (from `renv::status()`), `Using R … (lockfile was generated with R 4.6.0)` (when R starts), or `PROBLEM - install R 4.6` (step 8) | Your R isn't R 4.6. Install R 4.6 (step 1). If CRAN's download page already offers a newer R, take the newest R 4.6 from CRAN's earlier versions: <https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/macosx/sonoma-arm64/base/> (Mac with an Apple chip), <https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/macosx/big-sur-x86_64/base/> (Intel Mac) or <https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/old/> (Windows). Then start a console with R 4.6 (Interpreter picker → **New Console Session…**) and run `renv::restore()` again. |
| `uv: command not found`, or "not recognized" | Close the terminal window, open a new one, and try again. |
| `git: command not found` | Repeat step 3. |
| `Could not resolve host: github.com` (in the `fatal` line after `git clone`) | Git couldn't look up where `github.com` is, so it downloaded nothing. The command you typed isn't the cause. At HFR this happens when Git is installed on a network drive, such as `K:`: Git has to be on the computer's own disk. To see where it is, run `where.exe git` in PowerShell. If the answer starts with `K:` or another network drive, uninstall Git and install it again (step 3) in a folder on `C:`. If the computer doesn't let you, do the setup on an HFR laptop or on your own computer. Your own computer is fine for this site's practice data, which is synthetic; real study data stays where [Where HFR data lives](real-data.qmd#where) says. |
| Python can't find `pandas` in Positron | Start a console with the `.venv` Python: Interpreter picker → **New Console Session…** (step 7). |
| Anything else | Copy the whole error message and send it to your project lead. No project lead? Click **Report an error** on this page: it opens an email that already names the page (see [Getting help](using-this-site.qmd#getting-help)). |

## Other editors {#other-editors}

- **RStudio** (<https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/download.html>) is great for R. It can run Python too, but Positron is simpler when you use both.
- **VS Code** (<https://code.visualstudio.com>) works too: install the R and Python extensions.

Everything else on this page stays the same.
